title: Parashara puts out the fire
hookLine: the Vishnu Purana's teller earns his story by giving up revenge
carry: kshama: the purana's teller put down his revenge
tomorrow: Maitreya's first question is huge: where did the world come from?
last: THE SAME LORD IN EVERY BEING.

lines: A FIRE TO BURN THE DEMONS.
cards: The Vishnu Purana is told by a sage, Parashara, to his student Maitreya. And near the start, Parashara tells how he came to know it.
When he was young, he learned that his father had been devoured by a rakshasa, a man-eating demon, sent, he heard, by Vishvamitra.

Wild with anger, Parashara began a fire sacrifice to destroy the rakshasas, and they began to burn by the hundreds. Then his grandfather came to him: Vasishtha, the same sage whose staff once stopped Vishvamitra's army.
He said, roughly: enough, child. Let your anger go. Anger is the passion of fools; the wise don't keep it.

teach.h: PULASTYA: YOU WILL TELL THE PURANAS.
teach.b: What happened next is the point. Another great sage, Pulastya, arrived, pleased that Parashara had chosen to forgive, and blessed him: you will tell the Puranas, and know the gods truly.
So the man who tells the whole Vishnu Purana, Prahlada's story included, earned it by putting out a fire. Vasishtha's reason is worth keeping.
In the telling, he says anger destroys what a person builds with long effort: their good name, their tapas. And he'd know. He was the one who stopped an army with a staff.
He had the power, and he chose to put it down.
Hindus call this kshama: forgiveness, patience under wrong, counted among the marks of dharma, the right way to live.
Now look back at two weeks. A sage who forced a king into the sky, remembered for a prayer that asks. A father who let his son find Brahman himself.
A sage who knew every mantra and asked for the self. A king who learned to ask the earth, not break her. Two brothers undone by a quarrel.
And Prahlada, seeing the Lord in every classmate. Here's where it meets now. The assembly is done; Sam and Priya said the chant together, and Nani cried.
But Priya is still burning about the guy who snickered at the Sikh senior's reading, and she's planning how to get him back.

teach.h: THE TELLER PUT OUT THE FIRE.
teach.b: The teller of the Purana knows that fire. His grandfather told him what to do with it.

how: Purana recitations at temples and homes often begin by naming who tells the text to whom; the Vishnu Purana is framed as Parashara answering his student Maitreya. Kshama, forgiveness, is listed among the marks of dharma.

o: a single hymn to Vishnu chanted at every sunrise
stories about Vishnu, told by a teacher, read in chosen parts
a book of rules for temple building, read cover to cover

games.q: the teller and his fire — tap the pairs.
p: the teller, who gave up revenge
told him to let his anger go

s: Parashara stopped his revenge sacrifice when Vasishtha counseled him
then Pulastya blessed him to tell the Puranas.
in the telling, Vasishtha praises anger as a sage's strength
he says anger destroys what long effort has built.
the Vishnu Purana is told as a teacher answering a student
Maitreya asks; Parashara answers, and the answers make the book.

games.q: your kid asks why it matters who tells the Vishnu Purana. what's a fair answer from today?
o: the teller, Parashara, gave up his revenge first; the Purana came after he forgave.
he was the strongest fighter among the sages, so people listened.
it doesn't matter; only the stories count.
games.why: Vasishtha told Parashara to let his anger go; he stopped the fire, and Pulastya blessed him to tell the Puranas. kshama comes before the story.

practice: Bring to mind one wrong you're still carrying, small is fine. If you pray, offer it, silently, the way Vasishtha asked: enough; I let this anger go. If you don't pray, say it to yourself plainly.
You don't have to feel warm. Just notice the heat, and set it down for the rest of the time, the way Parashara stepped back from the fire.

wordCard.voice: The Vishnu Purana: stories centered on Vishnu, told by the sage Parashara to his student Maitreya, after he chose to forgive.

carryVoice: Your line: kshama, the Purana's teller put down his revenge before he told a word. Two weeks, gathered.
